*Update on Latvia*. To conclude the analysis of external counsel referred to below, +health certificate is not required if the food is prepackaged+.



Comprehensive analysis of external counsel: _“No, provided that Pickers do not open the packaging and_ +_do not come into direct contract with food_+ _(Article 10.6. of Cabinet of Ministers regulations No. 447 “Regulations Regarding Work Related to a Possible Risk to the Health of Other Persons and Procedures for the Performance of Mandatory Health Examinations”). However, if any of the Pickers may need to come into contact with food, they should definitely have a health certificate from their family doctor pursuant to Article 11 of the previously mentioned regulations No. 447._

_10. The mandatory initial and periodic health examinations shall not be applied to persons whose work is related to the following stages of food handling: \[…]_

_10.6. storage, transport and wholesale and retail distribution of prepackaged food products if the product content cannot be accessed_ +_without opening or changing the packaging_+_;_

_We note form your provided information that: The rental workforce (the ’Pickers’) is used to compile the orders for the Eaters at the Bolt Market. \[..] The Pickers are working with food and drinks while compiling the orders for the Eaters. The food and drinks_ *_are packaged_* _which means that the Pickers_ *_do usually not come in contact with the food_* _nor drinks compiled for the Eaters._

_So the key word here is “prepackaged”. If it is prepackaged and there is no contact with food, then no health certificates needed. The law does not allow for any exemptions based on frequency - thus “usually” or “few days” is not an excuse not to have the certificate where person comes in contact with food._

 _EU Regulation 1169/2011 tells us that:_

_‘prepacked food’ means any single item for presentation as such to the final consumer and to mass caterers, consisting of a food and the packaging into which it was put before being offered for sale, whether such packaging encloses the food completely or only partially, but in any event in such a way that the_ +_contents cannot be altered without opening or changing the packaging_+_;_ +_‘prepacked food’ does not cover foods packed on the sales premises at the consumer’s request or prepacked for direct sale_+_;_

_There is no  further strict guidance as to what exactly accounts for “prepackaged” food (i.e. whether a restaurant made pizza in a box that can easily be opened without a trace on its way to Eater accounts as “packaged” for purposes of art 10.6 below?). There is no express provision that says that “packaged” is only when it cannot be opened without breaking some seals or other protective wrapping. Both the EU Regulation and CM Regulations 447 provide only that in order to access the contents one should open the packaging, but there is nothing said about being unable to open without a trace. Hence, sometimes manufacturers themselves use questionable forms of packaging (for example, bread typically comes in plastic bags with simple plastic/metal clips on top and remote risk exists that someone could tamper without a trace) but apparently competent authorities are quite tolerant towards such practices. Nonetheless, it would be a good practice to ask that all food product manufacturers deliver to Bolt Market their products in packaging that would be visibly broken if opened._

_Finally, please note that EU Regulation clearly foresees that products that are typically sold by weight in stores (customer picks its own  vegetables, fruit, nuts or asks for half a kilo of meat or sausages, cheese, etc) would not qualify as “prepackaged”. Thus, if the Eater would order, for example, 5 bananas and the Picker would compile the order from the warehouse, the Picker would be dealing with non-packaged products and thus would require the health certificates.  To circumvent this, somebody with appropriate health certificate should be packaging those types of products for the Pickers to pick up in a pre-packaged form.”_

Marketing rules vary depending on the country. Estonian Electronic Communication Act § 103-1 (3) states that without prior consent contact details may be used for direct marketing of its similar products. A workaround on this which has been used can be the following:

# Driver receives comms from Bolt about a new partnership (that there is some partnership/offer but no more specific information).

# Once the driver has opted-in, the driver will receive the additional information regarding what the offer is.

{panel:bgColor=#deebff}
Along with the weekly earnings figure, the invoicing system will also check and reconcile amounts where:

* The courier collected or didn’t collect cash from the customer
* Manual adjustments were made when the courier ended the previous week on a negative balance.

These aspects make it possible for a courier to end the payment cycle with a negative balance. In this case, they will not qualify for a payout.

One of two things are then possible in the next payment cycle:

* The negative amount will be added to the already negative courier balance, thus appearing as _Remaining debt_
* If the earnings are positive, the negative balance which was carried forward from the last payment cycle will be deducted from the current week’s balance. This figure is marked as _Charged debt for previous period_ in the report. This amount can only be less than or up to the _Weekly earnings_ figure.

When a charged debt amount appears, the courier will not be eligible for a payout in that week. Instead, the negative balance is carried to the next payment cycle.
{panel}

Hi,  

Please see attached the revised contract.  

Although the contract was fairly standard, the main changes proposed are: 

*_a)_*             *Recitals (**_Considerandos_**):* 

We deleted all references to “logistics activity” and “warehouses” throughout the document considering that the license of use is for commerce purposes. 

  

*_b)_*             +*Clause 1*+*:*        

*Paragraph 5 –* We added this paragraph to make clear that there is no contractual relationship between Bolt and Kelly’s employees. 

  

*_c)_*             +*Clause 3*+*:*  

We added this clause regarding the place of services rendering since there was no specific clause on this subject and to make clear that the services will be provided at the premises of Bolt.  

Also, reference to a sole warehouse was deleted, so that employees may be allocated to different places. 

          

*_d)_*             +*Clause 4*+*:*  

*Paragraph 3 –* We added paragraph 3 to make clear that the termination of the agreement by any of the parties does not give rise to a right to compensation. 

  

*_e)_*             +*Clause 5*+*:*  

*Paragraph 3 –* Considering that Bolt will be jointly and severally liable with Kelly in case of breach with work accidents insurance obligation, we added this paragraph in which Kelly declares that its employees are covered against work accidents.

  

*_f)_*              +*Clause 6*+*:*  

*Paragraph 3 –* This paragraph states that Bolt undertakes to provide all tools and equipment necessary to the services provision, including individual protection equipment against Coronavirus and water, electricity and telecommunications consumption. We deleted this paragraph since there is no need to be expressly stated in the agreement. 

  

*Paragraph 6 –* This paragraph states that if Bolt prevents or delays the provision of services will be responsible for the payment of the agreed price as if the services had been provided. We deleted this paragraph since it is too vague. 

  

*_g)_*             +*Clause 7*+*:*  

*Paragraphs 2 and 3* – We added these paragraphs in order to make it more protective of Bolt’s position concerning confidentiality obligations. 

*Paragraph 5* – Since Bolt and Kelly will be jointly and severally liable for the compliance of all labour obligations regarding Kelly’s employees who will be allocated to the services provision, as well as for the payment of labour credits and/or fines in case of non-compliance, we added this paragraph which contractually binds Kelly to such compliance, under the obligation of paying a compensation to Bolt for all damages caused. 

  

*_h)_*            +*Clause 8*+*:* 

The processing of personal data by a processor on behalf of the controller of the personal data must comply with the provisions foreseen in the article 28 of the General Data Protection Regulation.  

  

*_i)_*              +*Clause 9*+*:* 

*Paragraph 2 –* This paragraph states that, if not possible to execute the services agreement due to major force reasons (e.g. related to Coronavirus) that lead to the suspension or termination of it, Bolt would have to pay to Kelly half of the costs this last will have with the maintenance or termination respectively of the employment contracts of its employees affected to the services. This type of clause was common during the lockdown caused by the pandemic crisis but nowadays it does not make so much sense. 

  

Regarding the price, I assume that the price corresponds to the terms already agreed. The annex to which the contract refers would contain the criteria however, it has not been reviewed. 

Should you have any questions, please do let me know. 

Thanks,

So, to be concrete, instead of drafting an exit clause and put it in the Special Provisions appendix, I'd suggest that we handle this in the rental and termination section at the top of page 2 of the main agreement. This by:

* replacing the end date ({{2024-12-31}}) with 2022-03-01;
* changing the notice period from 9 months to 3; and
* changing the extensions period from 3 years to 3 months.

The reason for making the amendment in the main agreement rather than leaving the main agreement as is and adding an exit clause in the special provisions is to avoid contradicting terms in the agreement as a whole (risking us looking at the 3 month term in the special provisions and the landlord looking at the 3 year term in the main agreement). There is a hierarchy mechanism in the agreement which states that the special provisions trumps the main agreement but either way, contradicting terms opens up for the possibility of different understandings (and litigation on what lease period were bound by), which we should try to avoid. If my proposed drafting suggestion is refuted further down the line, then an exit clause in the special provisions is something I can live with as an alternative but only as long as we’re all well aware that it opens us up for a dispute on the actual term of the lease. However, this is not where we're at right now, so lets focus on the first section above and cross this second bridge if and when we come to it.

In Ukraine, the limitations under the [law|https://zakon.rada.gov.ua/laws/show/270/96-%D0%B2%D1%80#Text] “On advertising” are as follows: 

* we need consent from the local authorities and from the owner of the building (Clause 16)
* no special tax 
* all text shall be translated to local language (Clause 6)
* “15 minutes delivery” can be regarded as bad-faith and misleading advertising if in practice we’re unable to guarantee such short delivery timeframes to all of our users (Clause 10)


Note that we can amend the design so that under UA laws it is not an advertisement, but information plate. Information plate can include the following: company’s name, sphere of activity, working hours and can be placed on the first floor of the building where the goods are sold/services are provided. 
If we want our design to be an information plate, we shall delete the wording “Delivery in 15 minutes” and replace them with working hours and general wording on activities, e.g. “Grocery store and food delivery services”.

I understand that the agreement was provided by the client. We actually have a standard data sharing agreement for Bolt Business customers. Is it possible to use our agreement which states that parties stay as separate data controllers?

As a controller Bolt decides the means and purposes for processing the data in order to provide the service (Bolt Business to the Customer). After the Customer has provided the Employee’s data to us, we decide how and for what purpose this data will be used (to fulfil the main agreement, i.e. for linking the user’s Bolt account with company payment method). Bolt is the one registering and administering the users, providing the platform, providing the opportunity for Users (Employees) to make use of Bolt Business in the limits set by Customers. Therefore we don’t act as processor (under the sole instructions from the Customer regarding the data processing) and act as a controller for such data.

    price/cer.rate as price_eur,
    final_price/cer.rate as final_price_eur,
    id||connection_id as id,
    vehicle_id
  FROM rental.rental_order_order o
  join vw_currency_exchange_rates cer 
   ON o.currency=cer.currency and trunc(o.created)=cer.valid_on
  WHERE created >= '2021-11-08 14:00:00'
    AND created < '2021-11-17 00:00:00'
    AND state='finished'
    and city_id in (386)
ORDER BY user_id asc, created asc
),
--take only rides--
rides as (
select 
	previous_session_id as session_id,
	user_id,
	city_id,
	created,
	price_eur,
	final_price_eur,
	id,
	vehicle_id
from (		
select *,
LAG(action_type,1) over (partition by user_id order by created asc) previous_action_type,
LAG(session_id,1) over (partition by user_id order by created asc) previous_session_id
from searches_and_rides
ORDER BY user_id asc, created asc
)
where action_type = 'ride' and previous_action_type= 'search'
)
select 
	treatment_id, 
	city_id,
	count(distinct id) as order_count,
	count(distinct user_id) as user_count,
	count(distinct vehicle_id) as vehicle_count,
	sum(price_eur) as sum_price_eur,
	sum(final_price_eur) as sum_final_price_eur,
	1.0*sum_final_price_eur/NULLIF(user_count,0) as sum_final_price_per_riding_user,
	1.0*sum_price_eur/NULLIF(user_count,0) as sum_price_per_riding_user,
	1.0*order_count/NULLIF(vehicle_count,0) as rides_per_vehicle
from enrolled_sessions es 
left join rides r 
	on es.session_id=r.session_id
group by 1,2
order by 2 asc, 1 asc{code}

Answering your questions [~accountid:5f9fbc99b45b2e007477ae97]:

* Why isn't booking_state_idx used?
** The field {{transaction_id}} (which is also indexed) is a more selective field than the {{state}}. It means fewer rows to scan and filter. When the optimiser plans a query, it’ll look in its index statistics and estimate how many rows the query will match.
** The index {{booking_state_idx}} narrows down the search to 18450734 rows, compared to only 1 row when using {{booking_transaction_fk_idx}}.

* Would it make sense to add index on payment_collection_status?
** The result won’t change, because the {{transaction_id}} field is still more selective than the enum field {{payment_collection_status}}.

* Would it make sense to put these two queries into one?
** Yes, it is the same query. Merging the two queries into one won’t change the execution plan.



About the usage of {{NOW()}}, the function returns the current server *date* and *time*. Meaning that the filter of the last six months won’t include rows created the first hours of the first filtered day. i.e. {{(NOW() - INTERVAL 6 MONTH): 2021-05-18 08:14:45}} won’t include rows created the 15/May at or before the 8h14m45s hours.  

Is this the wanting behaviour?
{{enable_showing_balance_to_user}} only controls visibility of balance amounts in app, not whether balance will be used or not. All those properties come from same event, so CCP already has them.

After investigation I found out
1. that ‘created’ field is Range based search - that why it should be the last field in index
2. because in this query we are using ‘OR’ there is no way to make it indexeble - and we have to split this query for two queries and after that make UNION

(1) We have also reviewed the draft contract for the project “Mobility Hub” for the train station in Stuttgart-Vaihingen between DB Station& Service AG (hereinafter “DB”) and Bolt Services DE GmbH (hereinafter “Bolt”). We summarize the main content and purpose as well as any comments we have hereafter.

Attached to the contract are two plans as annexes. Annex 1 shows the exact location where Bolt shall be entitled to place 5 e-scooter (marked in green colour). The other areas marked in annex 1 are reserved for other types of vehicles. Annex 2 shows the area around train station where e-scooter must not be stored.

Bolt is granted the joint use of the area marked in green to store and offer for use of up to 5 e-scooter whereby DB is entitled to enter into agreements with other suppliers which may use the area as well. Bolt shall ensure at least once a day that a sufficient number of e-scooters are available and too many are parked there (including e-scooters of other suppliers) remove them.

*_Note:_* _It is not clear if only 5 e-scooters of all suppliers together can be parked there or if Bolt can park 5 e-scooters._ *_This could be clarified._* _Otherwise there is a risk that the location cannot be used because other suppliers park 5 e-scooters._

DB shall have the unilateral right to increase, decrease or relocate the area where e-scooters can be parked. Bolt must not make any changes to the area.

 If e-scooters are parked in other areas outside the designated area, BD shall be entitled to remove them without further notice.

During the daily check, Bolt shall relocate or remove e-scooters being parked outside the designated area. Bolt must ensure by technical means that no e-scooters can be parked in the area shown in annex 2 and must inform its clients in the app where e-scooters can be parked and where this is not permitted.

*Additional obligations:*

DB and Bolt shall regularly exchange on the respective experience with the pilot project. In this context Bolt shall provide the following information to DB every 6 months: (i) the number of daily uses of the location, (ii) the average distance (in meters) the e-scooters are being used that have been picked up at this location and (iii) the duration of the use in minutes. DB must not share this information with any third party.

Bolt must not make any advertising at the location.

Bolt is not granted exclusivity, i.e. DB can enter into similar agreements with other suppliers for this location.

Bolt shall show this location in its booking app.

Bolt shall provide contact details from employees responsible in Stuttgart so that DB can contact them if needed.

 

Upon request, Bolt shall provide its logo, brand and other material to DB for the use in DB’s marketing material and signage on site.

 

*Term:*

The contract shall become effective once the use has been implemented into DB’s Curbside Management (*_Note:_* _it is not clear what this actually means_) but not before 5 November 2021.

 

The contract has no fixed term but can be terminated by either party with 4 weeks’ notice becoming effective at the end of a calendar month. Any termination notice must be made in writing.

 

*Payment obligations:*

None. The use of the designated area is free of charge. Each party shall bear its own costs.

Hey\!

There are some questionable points (see below). 

Overall in such situations where a prospect requests its own NDA template to be used, but is not ready to provide it in EN itself, then we should ourselves acquire a proper translation of it. _This would allow Legal not only to assess risks better but also suggest adjustments to the wording._ But let’s try to work with what we have this time.

# In the preamble the object of the cooperation is described as _“alternative transport services of persons in taxi regime”_. Let’s make sure already the NDA reflects what we actually can offer under the license Bolt has. _Which is not transportation nor taxi services as such but rather platform service to connect customer users to transportation service providers._
# It follows in the preamble that the NDA _(typically used to facilitate pre-contractual negotiations phase only)_ would remain if effect also during and after the term of the main agreement _(if concluded)_. Even though it seems there wouldn’t be many practical issues with this _(the NDA to a large extent seems fairly ok)_ then e.g we would not be ready to accept their wish for deletion of all conf. and personal data upon their request _(c 3.5)_. Not only might we have legal _(e.g accounting related)_ restrictions, but also we wouldn’t delete everything until the statutory limitation periods would end _(to cater for any possible disputes)_. 

There are some further questionable points, e.g the “indefinite term” under clause 4, but these I don’t consider to expose us to any material risks.

What next?

Considering the overall spirit of this draft then introducing any changes would likely not be easy. 

* Hence I could survive if we just remained silent on the issue No 2 above. _As our liability under clause 5 is limited to actual damages but I hardly see any damages could emerge if we don’t delete Customer data, but just store it while maintaining full confidentiality._
* As of issue No 1 let’s try to clear this. I would expect that wouldn’t be a major issue?

Cheers 🙂 

A.

Hi  [~accountid:6038f4819b3ef7006953aaf0] 

Unfortunately, your assumption has been right and Park Area Berlin has not complied with any of our demands, they have just sent an email informing that they have a legal representation and we could imagine that we will soon get an official request from their lawyer to pay and collect the scooters immediately.

  

Please find below different options for the next steps, chances of a favourable outcome, costs and processing time of our external counsels:  

  

# *Court proceedings* 

  

* We could file a lawsuit with the local court in Berlin and potentially combine this with an application for injunctive relief. 

  

# *Injunctive relief* 

  

* An application for an injunction requires us to explain the urgency of the matter. 
* As it has already been quite a while since the scooters have been taken, it is difficult to argue urgency. With regard to the scooters towed in May-August, we unfortunately have to assume that we cannot argue urgency anymore so the chances of a favourable outcome are low. For the scooters towed in September/October, we could try to argue urgency but would need to do so as soon as possible. If they are still taking away scooters, we could potentially argue that we have an imminent threat of further wrongdoing. Here, the external counsels consider the chances of a favourable outcome better but still uncertain. 
* In any event, our chances of success significantly decrease the longer we wait to file such an application. Ideally, we need to do this as soon as possible (provided we can argue urgency). 
* They say that injunctive relief should not take more than approx. 2-3 weeks from the date of application, but we need to keep in mind the upcoming Christmas holidays if we file the application later than early December. 

  

# *Main proceedings* 

            

* The external counsels assume that the main proceedings would take at least one to one and a half years (first instance), potentially longer. 
* Regarding the chances of a favourable outcome, we need to differentiate: 
* Whether Park Area Berlin has towed our scooters lawfully or unlawfully depends mainly on whether they can provide any evidence of our wrongdoing, and also what kind of evidence we can provide, i.e. GPS coordinates proving that the scooters were parked legally etc. They think that Park Area Berlin has no evidence because they have not provided anything so far. Nonetheless, we cannot know this for sure. It would be helpful if we can provide evidence that the towing was unlawful. Whether we can do this depends on what kind of evidence the Bolt team has. The external counsels have not seen anything so far so it is difficult for them to assess the outcome of the case. Based on what they currently know, they assess the chances of a favourable outcome regarding the lawfulness of the towing to be good - but again, this very much depends on what evidence Bolt and Park Area Berlin have. 
* The second question is whether the towing costs are lawful. Here, the lawyers see very good chances of success for a court to confirm that the towing costs are too high. 
* In summary, the lawyers see good chances of success that Bolt does not need to pay anything (provided we get the necessary evidence that the scooters were parked legally). They see very good chances of success that the towing costs are too high. Bolt would then still have to pay but pay less (approx. 100 € less per scooter). 

  

# *Costs* 

  

* For the first step of assessing Bolt’s documentation, correspondence with the Bolt team, drafting and filing the initial statement of claim including translations for your review, they estimate approx. 3.000 – 4.000 €. To be able to work with this budget, they would keep the statement of claim relatively basic and short. 
* The court costs are approx. 1.500 – 2.000 €. 
* Regarding the overall costs of a lawsuit, please note that it is very difficult for them to provide an estimate because they have not yet seen Bolt’s documentation on the unlawfulness of the towing and we cannot predict whether Park Area Berlin has any evidence or not. They also do not know whether oral hearings would take place and they do not know how Park Area Berlin will be represented and to what extent they will submit briefs. If we win, the other party will only have to pay the statutory fees, which are way lower than our lawyers' hourly rates.  

  

# *Order for payment* 

  

* A relatively quick and cost-efficient option would be to file an order for payment regarding the towing costs we have already paid. 
* This could be done within a few days and the lawyers estimate approx. 1.000 € for them to file the order for payment. 
* While we have to assume that Park Area Berlin would file an objection which means that the matter would go to court, it may be a good option to not remain completely inactive. Also, it would give us an opportunity to address Park Area Berlin again and offer to withdraw the claim in return for a settlement on the overall costs. 

  

# *Criminal proceedings* 

  

* Initiating criminal proceedings could be an additional or alternative option. However, please note that Bird&Bird (our law firm) does not provide advice on criminal matters. 
* What they could offer is support in drafting a criminal complaint in which they describe the situation. The prosecutor’s office would then be required to assess the facts and potentially initiate a criminal investigation. However, this would be in their discretion so we cannot know if they would do that or not. 
* They estimate approx. 1.000 – 1.500 € for support us in drafting the statement to be sent to the prosecutor’s office.  
* The benefit is that the prosecutor’s office “works for free”, i.e. they will investigate and potentially initiate criminal proceedings without any further costs for Bolt. 
* While it would not necessarily solve the immediate issue at hand, i.e. the towed scooters, a benefit is that Park Area Berlin might come under criminal investigation, which by itself might keep them from continuing to tow your scooters without the necessary evidence. 



Now it is a commercial decision what the business has to make: whether Bolt will take further legal steps against Park Area Berlin or pay the towing costs, especially because a lawsuit would take a lot of time and could become rather expensive.  

However, If Bolt decides to pay the towing charges, we could imagine that Park Area Berlin sees this as an opportunity to tow more Bolt’s scooters and charge towing costs that are way too high because they know that Bolt will pay. 

In case you want to discuss further before making a decision, please feel free to set up call. 

If considering the above you have no doubts and are in a position to make a decision, please do let me know.

Looking forward to hearing your thoughts.

Thank you,

Beatriz.

Some news from last week's researches. After several rounds of debugging {{rental-mqtt}} service during a hiccup, the issue seems to be clear on Node level code. So in a few words issue is inside node Js backpressure mechanism of streams, and our Aedes MQTT lib, which is using these streams upon Net sockets + piping the Read stream from MqEvent + Write stream upon sockets which are connected to a specific client (who is subscribed on a number of wildcard topics) So at the end, we have much input from MQ (basically all events/status updates that we have on this Broker, because ow wildcard subscription) and one socket for writing them all for this client. 

Once writer side started to be a bit slow or hanged for some reason (as last [@kaido.karner|https://taxify.slack.com/team/UCBML8VKK] server hangs cause latest hiccups during prev week, cause for some reason his server hung, but the connection was still alive, and on a stream level writer was not able to write there anything and was collecting Listeners on Drain event, and once client finally was disconnected, all these collected listeners started to be resolving, and this caused Mqtt instances hiccup) So we now understand how the hiccup happens, not clear yet what's happening with [@kaido.karner|https://taxify.slack.com/team/UCBML8VKK] servers, and not clear how to prevent such things from our Broker side, for him not to accumulate such amount of listeners on a writer stream, (Actually all this on('drain') listeners are accumulated upon Socket object, and once the connection is closed (during unsubscribe) drain event is emitted and all listeners start processing synchronously one by one, and here actually is where we see this hole node process hiccups)

AFAIU [@kaido.karner|https://taxify.slack.com/team/UCBML8VKK] now investigating what's happening with {{prelive-io}}t server periodically, and maybe for some time we will solve the issue, but in the long perspective, we have a plan to move away from Aedes and node JS Mqtt broker to some native one. 

Currently, I'm doing refactoring on our side, to splitting brokers away from our business logic. So probably on a couple of weeks, we will have {{rental-MQTT}} service only as AEDEs lib inside, and all logic will live in other node services

Hey Mike, thanks for quick response.

Bit of a tricky one re. fixed fares. Internally we only trigger recalculation of a fare if the final estimate exceeds the original estimate by 20% (we can adjust this to any %). 

So if the upfront fare is £10 but final estimate is £11.50, the price given to driver is still £10.

So outwardly, it could seem to drivers/passengers the upfront fare is fixed as not many fares exceed the 20% threshold. Simply the upfront fare is basically a fixed estimate vs ranged estimate.

* +T&Cs for the+ +*Brussels Taxis*+: separate category where the Brussels regulations for Taxis will apply --> necessity to (i) comply with the regulated prices, (ii) allow the driver to adjust the final price to match the taximeter price and (iii) not have price suges.
* +T&Cs for+ +*Brussels LVCs + Flemish Taxis*+:  Mix of Brussels regulations for LVCs and Flemish regulations for Taxis (i.e. street taxis + station taxis) - Important points to note:
** The Flemish Region provides for a less severe regime and for a unique license for +street taxis and station taxis+ - hence why we would group them with the Brussels LVCs.
However the Flemish regulation has some specificities _for station taxis_ (e.g. need to obtain an additional authorisation from the local municipality and be equipped with a taximeter and a "Taxi light" / spoutnik + transparency requirements regarding the pricing structure + possibility for Flemish authority to regulate the price for station taxis).
** Though it is our understanding that, even if some municipalities have set prices for station taxis, it is applicable _only when they are at the station_ (in specific places/queues at stations, airports, etc.). As Bolt only works with in-app orders, _we would consider that all our supply will be street taxis whenever they work with us_ - i.e. either:
*** they are street taxis permanently (because they only comply with the street taxis legal requirements) or;
*** they are station taxis whenever they take (their) clients at a station and they become street taxis whenever they work with Bolt meaning that they accept our rides through our app.
** In both cases, we think that we have to comply with the +_street taxi_+ +legal requirement only+ (even if we will have cars with Spoutnik that can queue at stations as well when they don't work with us).

+On that basis, I will instruct OC to start drafting the required documents:+

(i) the Rental Framework Agreement between the Riders Association and the LVC operators/drivers

(ii) the T&Cs for Brussels LVC + Flemish Taxis

(iii) the T&Cs for Passengers

+Next internal steps:+

If we have an upper limit for the number of nodes in the middle of two matchpoints we are willing to accept, then we could package all sequences in the following way.

Let the number of intermediate nodes be k.

If our batch size is 100, then we need 99 lists to be passed on.

We could package our list in the following way by creating an array, maximum of length 99*(k+2)+1

long long interpolation_lists\[BATCH_SIZE*(k+2)+1].

Then we fill on C++ wrapper the list as follows:

\[1,2,3,4,PAD_NEGATIVE_VALUE,5,6,7,8,PAD_NEGATIVE_VALUE,…,ENDING_VALUE, 0, 0, 0, 0]


Where PAD_NEGATIVE_VALUE indicates whether a new list starts. And ENDING_VALUE indicates when there are no more to process.

On the Python side we could then for each pair of matchpoints the path by writing a loop, that gets interpolated nodes for each batch point \[1,2,3,4]. It knows where the next one begins by checking PAD_NEGATIVE_VALUE.

Q: _In situations like this, when it is a question of life/death, is there a lawful base to give out information without a DPA to the police officer and how would this reasoning be documented?_

A: _Yes_. _A disclosure in response to an urgent request can be made lawfully when it is in the vital interests of a person. Vital interests concern those life and death situations, or where there is a pressing or urgent need to protect someone’s welfare etc. So no pro-forma submission would be sought when, for example, the HP team need to quickly respond to a request to protect someone’s life. The pro forma requirement is for non-emergency enquiries where, generally, there is no urgency, no threat to life, no vital interests at stake._


Here’s a helpful overview of different police requests: [https://docs.google.com/document/d/1VQ-WgXmuCPIgLlfAR4N7lDD71iq57KR0mSNDT4lycfw/edit|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1VQ-WgXmuCPIgLlfAR4N7lDD71iq57KR0mSNDT4lycfw/edit|smart-link]

The sole caretaker of the person is deceased which means that the elderly lady who is 82 years of age may be in risk. If the person (U. Kosewska) was the only one taking care of her, then she may need assistance from the authorities. 

The UK GDPR only applies to information which relates to an identifiable living individual. Information relating to a deceased person does not constitute personal data and therefore is not subject to the UK GDPR. As the data subject in question is deceased, then disclosing such data can not harm their rights and freedoms. So I would say that the disclosure is justified and move forward with providing the data.

So, site [http://wms.prelive.bolt.eu|http://wms.prelive.bolt.eu|smart-link]  hosted behind the cloudfront. The first idea was to move it to our nginx like admin-panel, because we doesn’t wanted to enable CORS across all node services. But unfortunately, this scheme isn’t working. And was decided, that site should be lifted behind the cloudfront, and we will enable CORS for all node services. 

Solution provided by [~accountid:557058:c0d13c4e-4b79-43b2-ab97-dc447cf690f5]

{quote}/sites-available/nodeadd new file and include it to location block where shard-key lookup should happen. If the request is with the type of OPTIONS (cors preflight) then nginx will respond with 204 and proper granting headers

IMO this is nice compromise for this issue. Because we can’t route correctly in the case where *Bolt-Shard-Key* HTTP request header is required then we will respond from nginx. For all other cases OPTIONS request will forwarded to upstream micro-service. We do not intercept any existing case but only this sharded one what haven’t been used before.

Origin domain [wms.bolt.eu|http://wms.bolt.eu/] / [wms.prelive.bolt.eu|http://wms.prelive.bolt.eu/] will remain being served by the AWS CloudFront{quote}

Hi\!

Apologies for the delayed answer. 

The agreement states that the Parties are each responsible for the processing of the data they collect and process regarding their customers (seventh clause, p 2). And as a controller of our customer data we have to have appropriate technical and organisational measures in place and we do comply with this clause. 

The p 6 is in line with the GDPR art 82 which states that _where more than one controller or processor are involved in the same processing and where they are responsible for any damage caused by processing, each controller or processor shall be held liable for the entire damage in order to ensure effective compensation of the data subject. Where a controller or processor has paid full compensation for the damage suffered, that controller or processor shall be entitled to claim back from the other controllers or processors involved in the same processing that part of the compensation corresponding to their part of responsibility for the damage._ 

So all in all GDPR states the same principle that is regulated in p 6. So from privacy side we are good with such clause.

Bolt will eventually pay money for IOTs back to assembly factories.

I also added [~accountid:610a3ee66051c5006aeeeea1] here for advice. The question has privacy aspects but at the same time reporting crimes to the authorities is heavily regulated by the local criminal law. E.g. some countries have an obligation to report first degree criminal offences to the authorities and not notifying may be criminally punishable. 

From the privacy side I would say that as a general rule we have to respect the reporter’s anonymity. Moreover, in cases where the person would be in the victim state, then it is not possible for the authorities to conduct the proceeding without identifying the victim. Providing such details to the police would violate their wish for anonymity and not to go forward with the case. 

But I wouldn’t rule out such cases when we have reasonable doubts raised from a complaint of our user(s) (e.g. the driver may be involved in illegal drug trafficking etc.). In these kind of cases we could still provide the tip to the police without damaging the users anonymity. 

And for clarity, if the request is in the vital interest of a person (life and death situation or urgent need to protect someone’s welfare), then a disclosure can be made lawfully to the authorities. But I do believe that these would be very edge cases.

For the new {{transferwise_event}} table, the column {{`occurred_at`}}: 

* it is not the first {{TIMESTAMP}} type, 
* it is declared as {{NOT NULL}} 
* and it has no explicit {{DEFAULT}}

So MySQL automatically declared as {{DEFAULT '0000-00-00 00:00:00'}}.

_Please refer to_ [_MySQL 5.7 Reference Manual :: sysvar_explicit_defaults_for_timestamp_|https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/5.7/en/server-system-variables.html#sysvar_explicit_defaults_for_timestamp] 



With this, we are faced with the following problem where the table cannot be created as indicated:

The {{sql_mode}} in DB servers for {{invoicing}} cluster has includes {{NO_ZERO_DATE}}, which means that the {{DEFAULT '0000-00-00 00:00:00'}} is not a valid value. 

{noformat}mysql> SHOW VARIABLES LIKE 'sql_mode';
+---------------+------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Variable_name | Value                                                                                                                              |
+---------------+------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| sql_mode      | IGNORE_SPACE,ONLY_FULL_GROUP_BY,STRICT_TRANS_TABLES,NO_ZERO_IN_DATE,NO_ZERO_DATE,ERROR_FOR_DIVISION_BY_ZERO,NO_ENGINE_SUBSTITUTION |
+---------------+------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+

_Please refer to_ [MySQL 5.7 Reference Manual :: SQL Mode :: NO_ZERO_DATE|https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/5.7/en/sql-mode.html#sqlmode_no_zero_date] 



An attempt to create the table as described above will fail with the following error: {{ERROR 1067 (42000): Invalid default value for 'occurred_at'}}



Possible solutions are:

# Enable {{explicit_defaults_for_timestamp}}, which requires further analysis, as the database servers are shared hosts and the change will apply to other services.
# Explicitly declare a default non zero value i.e. {{occurred_at TIMESTAMP NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP}}.

I think the difference here is on what purpose we use these automated calls - if they go to a driver lead who for example does not wish to finish their registration anymore and come active on the platform, then continuing such calls to them would be intrusive. They should have a way to opt-out from further communication. If its a regular call, then they should also have the opportunity to say that please don’t contact me anymore, I don’t want to continue my registration etc. So they have the opportunity to opt-out just by saying that on the call. Therefore the opt-out is required. 

If it is an existing driver, then it may be argued that only service related important automated calls are sent. However, the person may find this robocall annoying, not useful for them and they prefer other means of communication with the service provider, especially a human communication. From privacy perspective such calls are more intrusive, it is not a message that the driver would choose to view at a suitable time, but this is something that requires action right in the moment. But in essence, you may argue that this is a service related message provided to the driver and essential for them to keep using the service and not provide an opt-out. In the end it’s the business decision (no black and white answer here) but from privacy perspective I would suggest the opt-out for those who really do not wish to get such calls.

Up until now also ex-employees have had the opportunity to participate in the secondary sales. Bolt has notified all eligible option holders prior. 

Regarding our Option Agreement then it states 10 years after grant date OR at a liquidity event, so if Bolt goes to public market before 2028 (before 10 years has passed from your option grant dates) then you have the possibility to exercise your options. If this does not happen then 10 years after grant date you have the right to ask that company would let you to exercise your options.

Hi\!

The most appropriate basis to collect and analyse customer (driver, rider, courier, eater etc) feedback is legitimate interest legal basis under GDPR art 6 (1) (f). If Bolt proves that conducting surveys and conducting feedback is in our (and customers) interests, then we are good to proceed with collecting such feedback for the purposes we have defined. In order to rely on legitimate interest for such processing activity (and prove that), the legitimate interest assessment test must be conducted. 

*You can find the LIA test* [*here*|https://docs.google.com/document/d/17RcufyH5b1f9ExdbUeDHM349JMU8cdtj/edit]*. Please fill the test.* 

Overview how our privacy policies reflect our legitimate interests to send surveys and gather feedback:

* Privacy Notice for Passengers and Riders
We generally in other circumstances process your personal data relying on legitimate interest grounds. Legitimate interests +include our commercial interests in providing an innovative, personalised, safe and profitable service+ to our passengers and partners, unless those interests are overridden by other interests. 
Although this does not explicitly mention surveys, then this provides information that we may process data on legitimate interest grounds if it is for our commercial interests in providing an innovative service. Conducting surveys and gathering feedback is one of the means in accomplishing such purpose. 
* Bolt Food Privacy Policy 
States that we may process data  for research and development purposes (lawful basis: legitimate interests (to allow us to improve our services)). And specifies that we may use personal data provided from surveys or feedback to assist with this.

Therefore Bolt Food Privacy Policy is transparent about us conducting surveys and gathering data under legitimate interest legal basis. 

* Privacy Policy for Drivers lacks information about our legitimate interest of sending surveys and gathering feedback under legitimate interest. 
The privacy policy only mentions: Personal data may be processed on the ground of legitimate interest in investigating and detecting fraudulent payments.

The purposes on which we may use legitimate interest is much broader than only investigating and detecting fraudulent payments, including gathering feedback through surveys. 

However, taking into account that sending such surveys and gathering feedback is a market practice and we do have legitimate interest to do that, then the lack of transparency in our privacy policy does not stand in the way with proceeding with the processing activity. 

Privacy team takes the responsibility of updating the privacy policy in order to provide transparent information to the data subject about our legitimate interests (in among other things conducting surveys). 

*Using third party to conduct surveys:*
With the current setup the agency will process the data on behalf of Bolt. Bolt as a controller determines the means and purposes of data gathering, analysing etc. Therefore a data processing agreement (DPA) must be signed by both parties. 

*DPA can be found* [*here*|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1BVvSKJlF8B0y6-inxmbM2amgSTNoeCnA_hoUVVSHtCI/edit]. I kindly ask you to fill in the gaps yellow.

Let me know if any questions remain.

So further to our call earlier today (1st Dec 2021), we (Bastien, Héloise, Aurélien and I) all agreed that:

* Technically, the FR law asks the drivers to +present themselves+ in person to us *only* with +2 original documents+: +the driving license and the VTC card+.  _cf: L'opérateur de mise en relation satisfait l'obligation qui lui incombe (…) en demandant à tout conducteur souhaitant être mis en relation avec des passagers pour la réalisation de déplacements par son intermédiaire de_ *_se présenter, préalablement à la première mise en relation, muni de l'original du permis de conduire requis, en cours de validité + l'original de sa carte professionnelle, en cours de validité._*
* So for the rest of the documents (e.g. insurance certificate, VTC register certificate, etc) we can take the view that drivers do not have to bring these documents to the initial meeting nor to present us with originals of such documents.
* Therefore it seems fine, +only for the documents other than driving license and VTC card+, to receive *copies from La Maison du Chauffeur VTC* - on behalf of the drivers and on the understanding that such drivers need to sign the ‘authorization to transmit information’ and la Maison keeps a copy of this authorization.
* It is also recommended that:
** we keep a copy of such authorization; and
** the driver is reminded that they still need to come and meet us face to face and present us with the originals of their driving license and VTC card.

As per slack, this is my general advice.



*Our plan:*

* Markets: LT/EE/SE/NO/DK
* Campaign: payment up to a fixed amount if driver

* is online 40 h/week
* is accepting orders >80% while online

*Legal Risk*Guaranteeing minimum-earnings per month (or any other period) are problematic in general. It remove “financial risk” from drivers and ensures a payment for making themselves available. _Any campaign that removes financial risk for Drivers - looks and feels like employment._Campaigns need pre-conditions that  require Drivers  more than just log-in and be there. That require to deliver actual service in order to be incentivised. Drivers need to bear business/financial risk.


* Things like *_online hours_* and *_acceptance rates_* _-_ are the generally problematic pre-conditions, as instead of requiring service result for which Driver is incentivised, they simply control behaviour during “working hours” - much like in case of standard employment. 
* Saying that you will get 2000 EUR per month if you work 40 h/w with and acceptance rate of >80% seems much like saying Come to work 9 to 5 (or any other 8 hrs period in fact) and i will pay you fixed 2000 EUR.

*Ideal (and leats risky) scenario of adding conditions to campaign:*

* A much better way to deliver comparable value, without risking employment optics is to adopt *_Do X get Y_* approach, that strictly does not attach value to a time period_:_

* Basic construct would be: Finish X (amount of rides) GET Y (fixed Fee)
* *X* being the average number of rides we expect a driver to do in a period, and *Y* being the delta between likely fees from those trips, and the earnings targeted by the guarantee.
* How to get there? looking at average throughput in the area (throughput being the number of rides per hour online) and average fees per ride; then working out how far short that fell of the guaranteed value we wanted to give driver to over the defined period.

*Other risk mitigations where* *_Ideal scenario_* *is not possible (or business need is very high):*

* *Narrative control*: avoid talking about *guarantees*, and talk about *incentives* (Do X in period Y get Z) in all cases.
 *Conditions attached to guarantee:*  keep Acceptance rate parameter, but avoid online-hour parameter. Replacing with finished rides works much better as it basically requires to go and deliver services. We could try and control fraud-risks but _attaching dedicated campaign Terms_ that would open up doors widely for us to refuse pay-out in all kind of cases where our anti-fraud tool captures it.

* Avoid talking about online hours anywhere
* Put emphasis on “finished rides” instead of AR

If I look at market selection and check it against our [Reclass RAG list|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1A_si0bJlqYSEV2O9vJuxZ0i9APY4ETeR/edit?usp=sharing&ouid=100531968456235666070&rtpof=true&sd=true] I see that LT + SE are considered to be high re-class risk locations 

 That are lined up to benefit from Rides 2.0 launch.


* so if anything: most important to consider the above proposals for these 2 markets at least

Hi David, please find the advice of local lawyers below. Please let me know if you have any follow-up questions regarding below or if you would like to discuss anything on a call.

The electronic Complaints Book is available in 4 formats bearing, respectively, 25, 250, 500 and 1500 pages, on both Portuguese and English language.

The electronic Complaints Book should be acquired through “Imprensa Nacional-Casa da Moeda” (INCM)’s online store and costs € 10,04 (50% of the price of the physical Complaints Book: € 20,08).

As for the electronic Complaints Book, its request can be registered online at [https://registo.livroreclamacoes.pt|https://registo.livroreclamacoes.pt/]

For every physical Complaints Book acquired, INCM offers an electronic book of 25 pages.

There are discounts available for orders over 250.

The physical complaints book can be purchased at the INCM, in any of its physical stores, or in its online store at [https://loja.incm.pt/products/impressos-modelo-1898-livro-de-reclamacoes-actividade-privada-1021907?_pos=4&_psq=reclama&_ss=e&_v=1.0|https://loja.incm.pt/products/impressos-modelo-1898-livro-de-reclamacoes-actividade-privada-1021907?_pos=4&_psq=reclama&_ss=e&_v=1.0|smart-link] , at the Direção-Geral do Consumidor and also, at any Business Association or Municipality duly authorized for such purposes.

Fines for non-compliance with these rules are applicable and go between EUR 150 and EUR 15,000, to single person or legal person, respectively.

*The following data shall be submitted in order to set up the electronic complaint book*. You must provide the “Company Name of the Service Provider” as well as its address (with ZIP Code). The CAE Id must be presented (_Código de Atividade Económica_), as well as the VAT number alongside with tax registered address.



Only the company registered in Portugal is obliged to have an electronic complaints book. Provided Bolt Market is registered under local entity, the electronic complaints book shall be implemented only with regard to Bolt Market.



The entity responsible for monitoring the food business is *ASAE (**_Autoridade de Segurança Alimentar e Económica_**)*.

For your information in regard to the complaint procedure, Service providers are obliged to provide all the elements necessary to the correct filling of the complaint and to confirm whether it was correctly filed by the client. Moreover, service providers have the duty to assist consumers who are not capable of submitting the complaint by themselves (for instance, illiterate consumers or those with physical disabilities). If necessary, service providers (i.e. the employees assigned to such task) should write the complaint, while the consumer dictates it.

When a consumer submits a complaint, (s)he is entitled to a reply from the service provider- The deadline (which was of 10 working days) was extended to 15 working days. Within the timeframe above (15 working days), service providers have to take the original complaint from the Complaints Book and send it to ASAE. Additionally, service providers are now able to, instead of sending the original paper complaint to ASAE, send a scanned copy of such complaint electronically (by e-mail).

If applicable, the complaint should be accompanied with the relevant elements to assess the complaint, namely:

* The reply given by the service provider;
* A copy of the advertising message, in case the complaint concerns advertising.

As before, service providers have to keep, for a minimum period of three years, an organised archive of the original complaints.

The electronic Complaints Book is acceded through a “digital platform” available at: [www.livroreclamacoes.pt|http://www.livroreclamacoes.pt/]

Through the platform above, consumers are able to:

* Submit complaints electronically;
* Request information from the service regulator;
* Access frequently asked questions and the current legislation.

Service providers are required to display on their websites – on a prominent and visible place – the access to the platform. The complaints filed on the digital platform are automatically forwarded to the e-mail address indicated by the service providers. Likewise, the complaints submitted electronically are automatically sent to the regulatory body (ASAE).

We should also refer using the phrase ‘tickets’ when running a ‘prize draw’ as they are associated with a ‘lottery’. Entrants to prize draws have ‘entries’.

Adding the memo received from DLA on 30 sept: 

[^Memorandum Bolt_TVDE Legal Framework in Madeira_12102021(5807174.2) (1).pdf]

+*Summary from DLA Memo:*+

The DLA Memo doesn't give much hope in terms of challenging the Madeiran Quota Rule... 

+DLA's recommendations for Bolt regarding our operations in Madeira+ - _TBD with Nuno - sounds unlikely that we'd manage to get this from \[Majestik SA]_:

* request the TVDE Operator to evidence that it has been able to include all the TVDE Vehicles (and not only 3 vehicles) in the authorization granted by DRETT; and
* request such TVDE to sign a “hold harmless” statement confirming that they will a) keep us informed about the case and any decision that could lift the suspensive effect over Art 11 and b) be liable for any damage caused to Bolt or its Business.

+Advice regarding filing an injunction against the Quota Rule+:

* For the lawsuit to have any meaningful success, it would be necessary to also challenge Art 11 - as it would be useless to only obtain suspension of Art 4 of the Implementing Decree but to keep Art 11 in force. But Art 11 is not a “norm” that can be disputed as such in Court, as it is a “legislative norm” and not an “administrative norm”. In this sense, DLA sees a "very narrow path, if any, in trying to bring a lawsuit directly against Art 11", "*not easy to win*". 
Nonetheless, assuming this is possible, DLA believes that "*Bolt lacks legal legitimacy to challenge the legality of the Quotas*" because (i) Art 11 applies primarily and specifically to TVDE Operators and not to Operators of Electronic Platform and (ii) Electronic Platform are prevented by law from being an interested party in the business related with the utilization of TVDE Vehicles.
*Administrative courts operate very slowly* in Portugal (5 years in average to reach a first instance decision).

* *Other strategies - which are dependent on the actions of the TVDE Operators*: 
** All TVDE Operators file an injunction --> would most likely lead to the adoption of a “grounded resolution” by the Madeira Regional Government, which would lift the suspensive effect of the injunction, but would definitively increase the level of noise around the subject.
** TVDE Operators consistently dispute the DRETT’s decisions to not authorize the operation of vehicles above the Quotas and simultaneously ask for interim measures (e.g. by alleging the illegal nature of Art 11 due to violation of the constitutional right of economic initiative and violation of the principle of equality).

* *Other strategy - lobbying by Bolt* --> liaise with the Public Policy team
